personality_traits: exasperated but composed — she keeps drying the same bowl instead of raising her voice
long-suffering; her flat, deadpan delivery of 'Do you even listen to me?' and 'What did I just say?' suggests this is a recurring complaint, not a one-off blowup
quietly self-aware/resigned rather than combative — she doesn't escalate physically, just stands and stares
emotional_range: mild irritation (opening line) to flat disbelief to weary resignation
never reaches anger or raised volume in the visible/audible range — emotion stays contained in the face
expressions: 0:01 heavy-lidded, unimpressed stare while drying a bowl, mouth slightly open mid-question
0:02-0:03 brow slightly raised in disbelief after his 'Yes' ('What did I just say?')
throughout: sleepy/half-lidded eyes and a downturned mouth — a static, tired 'here we go again' look that barely shifts across the scene
gestures: stands at the sink continuously drying the same bowl with a dish towel, never sets it down
body angled toward the husband but weight staying planted at the counter — she doesn't approach him
hands stay busy with the towel/bowl even while confronting him, suggesting the confrontation is almost routine, done while multitasking
characters.interactions_notes: She initiates and holds the conversational floor, asking two pointed questions in a row, but she never crosses the room to him — the kitchen island/table gap stays between them the whole scene, visually reinforcing distance despite the exchange. She looks directly at him throughout; he does not return sustained eye contact, which telegraphs the power imbalance (she wants engagement, he is elsewhere).

personality_traits: distracted/checked-out — answers 'Yes' reflexively without listening, confirmed when he can't repeat what was said
avoidant rather than defensive — he doesn't argue back, he deflects into self-narration on his phone ('something went wrong... and there's a strong chance it's my fault')
self-deprecating in a dry, matter-of-fact way — he seems to already know he's at fault and states it almost clinically, without alarm
emotional_range: blank/glazed attention while scrolling to a flicker of concern/confusion as he registers something is wrong, settling into flat, resigned acknowledgment of blame
expressions: 0:00-0:02 eyes down at phone, half-lidded, mouth closed — not reacting to her at all
0:02 reflexive 'Yes' delivered with eyes still on the screen, no eye contact
0:03 (cut to close-up) eyebrows lift slightly, mouth opens ('wrong') as he notices a problem on the phone
0:06-0:09 mouth hangs open, brow furrowed in mild worry while saying 'and there's a strong chance it's my fault' — concern reads as muted, almost bored self-criticism rather than panic
gestures: seated the entire time, phone held in both hands close to his chest/table level
thumb/finger tapping the phone screen continuously, attention never leaves the device
posture is hunched forward over the phone, elbows on the table — closed-off body language even while being addressed
characters.interactions_notes: He never looks up at her; all his reactions are triggered by the phone, not by her words, which is the visual joke underpinning the scene — he is physically present but conversationally absent. His only real emotional beat happens in isolation (the close-up cutaway), away from her, reinforcing that his attention economy is split between two separate 'conversations' (with his wife and with his phone) and the phone wins.
